title: Prefill-Decode Disaggregation: Why Decoupling Compute-Bound TTFT from Memory-Bound Generation Rescues LLM Serving Fleets
summary: In conventional LLM serving systems like vLLM and TGI, a single GPU cluster handles both the prompt prefill phase (processing thousands of input tokens simultaneously) and the autoregressive decode phase (generating tokens one-by-one). Because prefill saturates GPU matrix compute cores (FLOP-bound) while decode is strictly constrained by High Bandwidth Memory read speeds (memory-bandwidth bound), co-locating them forces compute-heavy prefill bursts to preempt running decode batches, spiking Inter-Token Latency (ITL) and causing severe tail-latency stuttering. Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (PD Disaggregation) splits the inference cluster into two specialized tiers: dedicated Prefill workers optimized for high-FLOP matrix multiplication and dedicated Decode workers packed with high VRAM capacity. Once a prefill worker calculates the initial KV cache for a prompt, it streams the tensor slices across ultra-fast RDMA network fabrics to a decode worker, isolating Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) from token streaming throughput and slashing p99 latency by over 70%.
analogyTitle: The Real-Life Analogy: The Airport Express Check-in Counter vs. The Boarding Gate Queues
analogy:
Imagine an international airport handling thousands of passengers every hour.

Under a Co-located Architecture (The Combined Terminal Desk), a single airline agent must both verify bulky 10-page visa documents for new travelers arriving at the terminal (Prompt Prefill) and stamp boarding passes one-by-one for travelers stepping onto the plane (Token Decoding). When a tourist group of 50 passengers arrives with stacks of complex paperwork, the agent halts all boarding for 15 minutes to inspect the visas. Passengers already at the jet bridge are stuck in a suffocating standstill, missing departures (Inter-Token Latency spikes and stuttering streams).

Under a Prefill-Decode Disaggregated Architecture (Specialized Processing Terminals), the airline splits duties completely. A dedicated fleet of rapid passport verification desks (Prefill Tier) processes incoming travelers in bulk. The moment paperwork is validated, the digital travel record is sent over high-speed fiber tubes (RDMA KV-cache transfer) to dedicated flight concierges at the boarding gates (Decode Tier). The boarding gates do nothing except rapidly scan passenger barcodes at a steady 50 passengers per second without ever getting stalled by incoming paperwork.

sections.heading: 1. The Computational Mismatch: FLOP-Bound Prefill vs. Memory-Bound Decoding
sections.content:
Serving large language models involves two phases with polar opposite hardware bottlenecks:

• The Prefill Phase (Compute-Bound): When a prompt arrives, all input tokens are known simultaneously. The GPU performs matrix-matrix multiplications ($GEMM$) across the entire input sequence. This phase achieves near-peak Tensor Core utilization, saturating floating-point compute ($FLOP/s$) with high arithmetic intensity ($FLOPs/byte$).
• The Decode Phase (Memory-Bandwidth Bound): Generating output tokens occurs autoregressively. The model evaluates a single new token ($S_Q = 1$) against all historical Key and Value tokens cached in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM). This phase performs matrix-vector operations ($GEMV$), moving entire gigabytes of KV-cache tensors across the memory bus just to compute a single forward pass. Tensor cores sit idle waiting for memory loads, yielding an arithmetic intensity below $10\text{ FLOPs/byte}$.
• The Interference Penalty: When both phases share the same GPU, scheduling a prefill burst halts decode batches. Active streams suffer unpredictable latency bubbles, turning what should be a smooth 30 tokens/sec stream into an irregular, halting user experience.

sections.heading: 2. Decoupling the Pipeline: Dedicated Pools and KV-Cache Network Streaming
sections.content:
Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (PD Disaggregation) eliminates this interference by segregating workers into two distinct hardware pools:

• Dedicated Prefill Nodes: Sized for maximum matrix throughput. These instances use aggressive Tensor Parallelism ($TP = 4$ or $TP = 8$) to spread wide attention matrices across multiple GPUs, completing prompt ingestion and initial KV-cache construction in minimum Time-to-First-Token (TTFT).
• Dedicated Decode Nodes: Sized for high memory capacity and memory bandwidth. These workers maximize concurrent batch size ($B = 128+$) across many active streams. Because no compute-heavy prefill bursts ever run on these GPUs, decode batches execute with uninterrupted, deterministic rhythm, driving down Inter-Token Latency (ITL) variance.
• Sub-5ms KV Cache Streaming via RDMA: Once prefill finishes, the resulting KV tensors must transfer to a decode node. Using Kernel-Bypassing RoCEv2 or InfiniBand RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access), engines stream memory pages directly from prefill GPU VRAM to decode GPU VRAM over 400Gbps network fabrics in 2 to 5 milliseconds, completely bypassing host CPU memory bottlenecks.

sections.heading: 3. Independent Autoscaling and Predictable Production SLAs
sections.content:
Decoupling the execution pipeline transforms LLM cluster economics and reliability:

• Independent SLA Management: Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and Inter-Token Latency (ITL) become decoupled control variables. If an enterprise workload experiences a spike in 8,000-token prompt documents (e.g., automated document analysis), cluster orchestrators scale out the prefill pool without disturbing active decode workers.
• Elimination of Bubble Preemption: Monolithic schedulers rely on complex chunked prefill heuristics to interleave prefill slices between decode steps. This compromise restricts both prefill matrix efficiency and decode batch sizing. PD disaggregation removes the compromise entirely.
• Hardware Specialization: Because prefill demands raw compute while decode demands memory capacity, engineering teams can deploy heterogeneous hardware—for instance, high-FLOP FP8 accelerators for prefill and high-capacity HBM3e nodes for decode—maximizing cost efficiency per token.

takeaway: Co-locating compute-bound prompt prefill and memory-bandwidth-bound token decode on the same GPU causes prefill spikes to interrupt active generation streams. Prefill-Decode Disaggregation splits inference into dedicated hardware pools, streaming constructed KV caches across RDMA networks in milliseconds to deliver stable Inter-Token Latency and predictable Time-to-First-Token at enterprise scale.
